claims.text: The low-field magnetocaloric response of nanoscale non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type films or nanoribbons is predominantly controlled by nanoscale interface strain.
Disordered magnetic-domain configurations predominantly control hysteresis in these nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi-type materials.
Controlled post-deposition annealing will relieve interface and lattice strain without significant grain growth.
Strain-relieving annealing will improve magnetic-domain coherence.
Strain-relieving annealing will sharpen the magnetic or magnetostructural phase transition.
Strain-relieving annealing will enhance the magnetocaloric effect relative to the as-deposited state.
Strain-relieving annealing will reduce magnetic hysteresis relative to the as-deposited state.
As-deposited nanoscale films or patterned nanoribbons have a high density of grain boundaries.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type films possess intrinsic interfacial strain.
Interfacial strain and grain-boundary disorder broaden the magnetic transition and increase hysteresis in the as-deposited material.
Nanoscale dimensions enhance the influence of interfaces and strain-induced magnetic disorder.
Strain-induced disorder disrupts coherent magnetic exchange and broadens the thermomagnetic transition.
A broadened thermomagnetic transition suppresses the magnetocaloric response and increases hysteresis.
Strain relaxation promotes a more uniform magnetic-domain configuration and a narrower distribution of local anisotropies.
A more uniform magnetic-domain configuration enhances magnetostructural coupling.
Annealed samples will exhibit higher adiabatic temperature change or isothermal entropy change than as-deposited controls.
Annealed samples will exhibit a smaller magnetic hysteresis-loop area than as-deposited controls.
Annealing may slightly shift the transition temperature.
Heat-transfer limitations constrain the usable magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.
The proposed comparison is to be conducted at applied magnetic fields below approximately 200 mT.
